definition: ULTRA is a machine translation system created for five languages (Japanese, Chinese, Spanish, English, and German) in the Computing Research Laboratory in 1991.
details: ULTRA (Universal Language Translator), is a machine translation system developed at the Computing Research Laboratory, which can translate between five languages (Japanese, Chinese, Spanish, English and German). It uses Artificial intelligence as well as linguistic and logic programming methods. The main goal of the system is to be robust, to cover general language and to be simple to use. It uses bidirectional parsers/generators. The system has a language-independent system of intermediate representation, which means that it takes into account needs for expression (expression is one of the main elements of language) and it uses relaxation techniques to provide the best translation. It used an X Window user interface.

explainer.lead: ULTRA is a machine translation system created for five languages in 1991 at the Computing Research Laboratory. It matters as an early system combining AI with linguistic and logic programming methods for robust general-language translation.

tiers.eli5: Like a translator that sits between five languages and passes every sentence through one common middle step.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use its bidirectional parsers and generators over a language-independent intermediate representation; a pitfall is that robustness and general-language coverage, not narrow specialization, are the design goals.
tiers.paperLevel: A machine translation system using AI plus linguistic and logic programming methods, with bidirectional parsers and generators and a language-independent system of intermediate representation, aiming to be robust, cover general language and be simple to use.

explainer.example: An English sentence is parsed into the language-independent intermediate representation and generated out as German.
